title: In-ear monitor (IEM): parametric design template (theory-only)
description: A 10 mm class dynamic micro-driver in an in-ear shell, loaded by the IEC 60318-4 occluded-ear simulator (the in-ear coupler) or the ITU-T P.57 Type 4.3 canal from its reference plane. Modelled: the front volume between the diaphragm and the nozzle; the nozzle bore with an optional mesh or damper at its outlet and the area step into the canal; the ear-tip seal, as sealed, as an equivalent leak tube through the tip (typical and loose fits) or as a custom tube; the rear volume behind the driver with a pressure-relief vent that can carry a mesh. Anchors: the driver's moving mass, force factor, coil resistance, diaphragm area and resonance are the in-ear example of Poldy, Headphone Fundamentals, AES 120th Convention tutorial (2006), Fig. 20, a simulation example rather than a measured driver; the leak tubes are two of the sizes Groon et al. (Ear and Hearing 36, 2015) put through foam tips, 13 mm long. Estimates: the mechanical Q, the shell volumes, the nozzle and vent geometry and every tolerance. The fit states are illustrations, not population statistics. Not modelled: the tip's own compliance and mass, the canal wall of a real ear, diaphragm break-up. docs/templates.md gives the sources and what the defaults produce.

driver_fs_Hz.label: Resonance fs (free air)
driver_fs_Hz.description: Poldy (2006), Fig. 20: mechanical resonance of the in-ear example.

tolerance.source: estimate (as the over-ear driver's datasheet tolerance)

driver_Qms.label: Mechanical Q (Qms)
driver_Qms.description: Estimate. Poldy's example has no mechanical loss (Rms = 0); a film suspension has some.

driver_Re_ohm.label: Coil resistance Re
driver_Re_ohm.description: Poldy (2006), Fig. 20; a 16 ohm rated driver.

tolerance.source: estimate (as the over-ear driver's datasheet tolerance)

driver_Sd_cm2.label: Diaphragm area Sd
driver_Sd_cm2.description: Poldy (2006), Fig. 20: 0.8 cm2, a diaphragm of about 10 mm.

driver_Qes.label: Electrical Q (Qes)
driver_Qes.description: Qes = 2 pi fs Mms Re / Bl^2, from the force factor.

driver_diameter_mm.label: Effective diaphragm diameter
driver_diameter_mm.description: Diameter of a circle of area Sd; the cross-section draws the diaphragm and the shell this wide.

driver_Le_uH.label: Coil inductance Le
driver_Le_uH.description: Not given in the source example; 0 leaves it out.

driver_Xmax_mm.label: Linear excursion Xmax
driver_Xmax_mm.description: Estimate for a 10 mm film diaphragm.

front_volume_cm3.label: Front volume (diaphragm to nozzle)
front_volume_cm3.description: Air between the diaphragm and the nozzle inlet (estimate).

front_depth_mm.label: Front volume depth
front_depth_mm.description: Depth of a cylinder as wide as the diaphragm holding the front volume; the cross-section draws it.

nozzle_diameter_mm.label: Nozzle bore
nozzle_diameter_mm.description: Inner diameter of the sound tube through the nozzle (estimate).

nozzle_length_mm.label: Nozzle length
nozzle_length_mm.description: From the front volume to the tip of the nozzle (estimate).

nozzle_mesh_rayl.label: Nozzle mesh or damper (0 = none)
nozzle_mesh_rayl.description: Specific flow resistance, MKS rayl, of a mesh across the nozzle outlet, over the bore area.

canal_diameter_mm.label: Canal diameter at the tip
canal_diameter_mm.description: The bore the nozzle opens into, for the area-step inertance: 7.5 mm is the IEC 60318-4 main cavity (docs/ear-loads.md).

fit.label: Ear-tip fit
fit.description: Leak past the ear tip as an equivalent tube from the canal to the room. The slight and loose tubes are 0.020 and 0.040 inch, two of the sizes Groon et al. (2015) inserted through foam tips; the effect on low-frequency measurements became significant above 0.010 inch. Which leak is typical of a person is not established.

custom_leak_diameter_mm.label: Custom leak tube diameter
custom_leak_diameter_mm.description: Used when the fit is Custom.

leak_length_mm.label: Leak tube length
leak_length_mm.description: 13 mm: the length of the tubes in Groon et al. (2015).

damping_rayl.label: Damping behind the diaphragm (0 = none)
damping_rayl.description: Specific flow resistance, MKS rayl, of the cloth or felt over the driver's rear openings, between the air space behind the diaphragm and the rear volume (estimate). It damps the diaphragm's resonance on the air springs.

damping_area_cm2.label: Open area under the damping
damping_area_cm2.description: Total area of the driver's rear openings under the damping (estimate).

driver_back_volume_cm3.label: Air space behind the diaphragm
driver_back_volume_cm3.description: Volume inside the driver between the diaphragm and its rear openings; 0.15 cm3 is the rear cavity of Poldy's (2006) example.

back_depth_mm.label: Air space depth
back_depth_mm.description: Depth of a cylinder as wide as the diaphragm holding the air space behind it.

rear_volume_cm3.label: Rear volume
rear_volume_cm3.description: Air in the shell behind the driver, between its damped rear openings and the vent (estimate).

rear_depth_mm.label: Rear volume depth
rear_depth_mm.description: Depth of a cylinder as wide as the diaphragm holding the rear volume; the cross-section draws it.

vent_mesh_rayl.label: Vent mesh (0 = open hole)
vent_mesh_rayl.description: Specific flow resistance, MKS rayl, of a mesh over each vent. 260 rayl is the Saati Acoustex grade of the materials database (saati_acoustex_260, unverified); with it the vent relieves the rear volume below about 25 Hz. An open hole resonates with the rear volume and blocks the diaphragm near its Helmholtz frequency.

choices.label: ITU-T P.57 Type 4.3 canal from its reference plane

drive_mW.label: Drive power into the rated impedance
drive_mW.description: Every level states its drive: this is the power into the rated impedance. Warnings are checked at this drive.
